definitions.explanation: A person who acts foolishly or comically to entertain others. Can refer to a professional entertainer or someone behaving in a clownish manner.
The act of behaving comically or playing the fool for amusement.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はクラスの{道化|どうけ}だ。
{王様|おうさま}の{前|まえ}で{道化|どうけ}が{芸|げい}を{見|み}せた。
examples.english: The jester performed in front of the king.

examples.japanese: いつも{道化|どうけ}を{演|えん}じていた{彼|かれ}が、{突然|とつぜん}{真剣|しんけん}な{顔|かお}になった。
examples.english: He always played the clown, but suddenly his expression turned serious.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}の{道化|どうけ}ぶりに{皆|みな}が{笑|わら}った。
{場|ば}の{空気|くうき}を{和|やわ}らげようと{道化|どうけ}を{演|えん}じたが、{誰|だれ}も{笑|わら}わなかった。
examples.english: I played the fool to lighten the mood, but no one laughed.

notes:
USAGE:
{道化|どうけ} can refer either to a person (clown, jester) or to the act of clowning. The compound {道化師|どうけし} specifically means a professional clown or jester.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {道化|どうけ}を{演|えん}じる (to play the fool)
- {道化師|どうけし} (clown; jester)
- {道化|どうけ}{芝居|しばい} (farce; clownish act)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In traditional Japanese performing arts, comic roles have a long history. {道化|どうけ} is sometimes used to describe the comedic servant characters in {狂言|きょうげん} plays.
